clauses.text:
(a) For flexural members of special moment frames, at any section and for both top and bottom reinforcement, the amount of reinforcement shall be not less than 0.25(f'c/fy)bwd or 1.4(bwd/fy), whichever is greater and the reinforcement ratio ρ shall not exceed 0.025. At least two bars shall be provided continuously both top and bottom. The positive moment strength at
the face of the joint shall be not less than one-half of the negative moment strength provided at that face as shown in Figure 6.8.2. Neither the negative nor the positive moment strength at any section along the member length shall be less than one-fourth the maximum moment strength provided at the face of either joint.
clauses.notes:
f'c - Specified compressive strength of concrete.
fy - Specified yield strength of reinforcement.
bw - Web width of the flexural member.
d - Effective depth of the flexural member (distance from extreme compression fiber to centroid of tension reinforcement).
Flexural member - A beam-type member primarily resisting bending.
Special moment frame - A moment-resisting frame designed to meet special seismic detailing requirements.
ρ (reinforcement ratio) - The ratio of the area of longitudinal tension reinforcement to the product of bw and d.

"The positive moment strength at the face of the joint shall be not less than one-half of the negative moment strength provided at that face as shown in Figure 6.8.2. Neither the negative nor the positive moment strength at any section along the member length shall be less than one-fourth the maximum moment strength provided at the face of either joint." - This part will be checked later.

clauses.text:
(b) For flexural members of special moment frames, Lap splices of flexural reinforcement shall be permitted only if hoop
or spiral reinforcement is provided over the lap length. Maximum
spacing of the transverse reinforcement enclosing the lapped bars
shall not exceed d/4 nor 100 mm. Lap splices shall not be used; (i)
within the joints, (ii) within a distance of twice the member depth
from the face of the joint, and (iii) at locations where analysis
indicates flexural yielding caused by inelastic lateral displacements of the frame. Not more than 50% of the bars shall be spliced at one location;
clauses.notes:
Special moment frame - A moment-resisting frame designed to meet special seismic detailing requirements.
Lap splice - A connection of two bars by overlapping them a specified length so that force is transferred between them.
flexural reinforcement - In general, reinforcement of a beam.
Hoop reinforcement - Closed ties or continuously wound ties enclosing the longitudinal reinforcement.
Spiral reinforcement - Continuously wound reinforcement in a helical form enclosing the longitudinal bars.
Lap length - The length over which two bars overlap to transfer force.
Transverse reinforcement - Hoops or spirals placed perpendicular to the longitudinal bars to confine the lap splice region.
d - Effective depth of the flexural member.
Lapped bars - Bars connected by overlapping within a lap splice.
Flexural yielding - The condition where the reinforcement reaches its yield stress under bending.
Inelastic lateral displacement - Lateral movement of the frame beyond the elastic range, typically under seismic loading.

"(iii) at locations where analysis
indicates flexural yielding caused by inelastic lateral displacements of the frame." - This part will be done later.
